title: Essential surjectivity of the canonical Galois stalk functor
statement: Let $K,K_s,\Omega$ be fields in $\mathrm{Type}\,u$, with compatible algebra structures $K\to K_s\to\Omega$, $K_s$ a separable closure of $K$ [def-pd-separable-closure], and $\Omega$ algebraically closed. Let $J$ be the small etale topology on $\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], let $p$ be the point defined by $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, and let $p^*$ be its set-valued geometric stalk functor [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Put $G=\operatorname{Gal}(K_s/K)$ with the Krull topology and $w=\max(u+1,v)$. Let $U$ be the forgetful functor from discrete continuous $G$-sets in $\mathrm{Type}\,w$ to sets. Let $T:\operatorname{Sh}(J,\mathrm{Type}\,w)\to\operatorname{DiscreteContAction}(\mathrm{Type}\,w,G)$ be a functor, and $j:T\circ U\cong p^*$ a natural isomorphism satisfying the canonical germ formula. The canonical germ formula is: for a sheaf $F$, $g\in G$, a $K$-automorphism $\tau$ of $\Omega$ with $\tau\circ i=i\circ g$ for the embedding $i:K_s\to\Omega$, an etale $K$-scheme $X$, lifts $x,x^{\prime}:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ over $K$ with $x^{\prime}=x\circ\operatorname{Spec}\tau$, and $z\in F(X)$, $j_F(g\cdot j_F^{-1}(\operatorname{germ}_x z))=\operatorname{germ}_{x^{\prime}}z$. Then $T$ is essentially surjective: for every discrete continuous $G$-set $M$ in $\mathrm{Type}\,w$, there is a sheaf $F$ and an equivariant isomorphism $T(F)\cong M$.

proof.text: Each orbit of a discrete continuous G-set M is finite: its stabilizer is open, and the quotient of the compact group G by an open subgroup is finite. Represent the orbit in Type u. Apply the etale-field/G-set equivalence to produce an etale K-scheme X with that small geometric-point G-set.

The representable h_X is a sheaf. Lift its values to Type w. Its stalk is the Omega-points of X by the representable-stalk isomorphism. Finite separable residue fields identify these with its Ks-points. The assumed germ formula identifies the actions under j, so T(h_X) is equivariantly isomorphic to the orbit.

Take the coproduct of these sheaves, indexed by the orbit set of M in Type w. Stalks preserve coproducts: Mathlib Point.Skyscraper makes sheafFiber left adjoint to the skyscraper functor. Naturality of j identifies the underlying maps of the images of the coproduct injections with the stalk injections; they are equivariant since T is a functor to G-sets. The induced underlying bijection from the disjoint union of orbits is therefore an equivariant isomorphism to T of the coproduct. This disjoint union is M. If M is empty take the empty coproduct; no Type u coproduct scheme is needed.
